why: Raising the water only removes rocks, so 'can I still cross at level h' is monotone: true up to some height, then false. Binary search h. For a fixed h, landing on every surviving rock is optimal, because splitting a jump never increases its length and (a + b)^2 >= a^2 + b^2, so feasibility is one greedy scan of the gaps.
hints: If you can cross at water level h, can you cross at any lower level? What does that monotonicity let you do?
For a fixed level, which rocks should you use? Every one still above water: a long jump costs more energy than the same distance in two hops, and short hops never break maxJump.
Binary search h in [0, 10^9]; check(h) walks 0 -> surviving rocks -> width, failing on a gap > maxJump or total squared gaps > maxEnergy. O(numRocks * log 10^9).
pitfalls: A rock is usable while level <= height (submerged only if the water is strictly higher).
Return -1 if even level 0 fails, and 10^9 if the top level still works.
Energy totals reach 10^18; Python is fine, but in other languages use 64-bit and stop early when the sum exceeds maxEnergy.
Do not forget the final jump to the right bank.
statement:
A river runs from x = 0 (left bank) to x = width (right bank). Rock i stands at position x[i] (strictly between the banks, sorted ascending) and has height heights[i].

You jump from the left bank, possibly via rocks, to the right bank. A jump from position a to position b costs (a - b)^2 energy, and no single jump may be longer than maxJump. The total energy must be at most maxEnergy.

Before you start, the water rises to some level h. A rock with height < h is submerged and cannot be used; a rock with height >= h is still usable. Return the largest water level h at which you can still cross. Return -1 if you cannot cross even at level 0, and 10^9 if crossing is possible at every level up to 10^9.

Example: width = 10, rocks at x = [4, 7] with heights = [3, 5], maxJump = 10, maxEnergy = 40.

  • Level 3: both rocks usable. Path 0 -> 4 -> 7 -> 10 costs 16 + 9 + 9 = 34 <= 40. Possible.
  • Level 4: the rock at 4 (height 3) is submerged. Best path 0 -> 7 -> 10 costs 49 + 9 = 58 > 40. Not possible.

The answer is 3.
